di01_1_1.texto: Sit down. They call me El Diablo. Not because of what I do: because I never give a warning.
di01_1_1.oido: Sit down, they call me el diablo, not because of what I do, because I never give a warning.

di01_1_3.texto: I give names. You cross them out. No letters, no threats, no second chances.
di01_1_3.oido: You give names, you cross them out, no letters, no threats, no second chances.

di01_1_4.texto: The first one: Fat Tano. He drinks at La Gaviota Bar with two heavies. When you leave, none of them should be standing.

di01_4_1.texto: Not one word too many, not one shot too few. I like it.
di01_4_1.oido: Not one word too many, not one shot too few, I like it.

di01_4_2.texto: Come back when you want another name. And check the board by the bar: that's where I hang the small jobs.

di02_1_1.texto: The Lobo brothers owe me something you can't pay back with money. And somebody has told them.

di02_1_2.texto: They're loading a sedan at the Hierro Viejo Scrapyard. Make sure they don't get out of Puerto Bravo.

di02_4_1.texto: The Lobos don't run any more. Good.

di02_4_2.texto: What worries me is who tipped them off. We'll know soon enough.

di03_1_1.texto: Rubén Saldanya. He worked for me and sold my names to the highest bidder.

di04_1_2.texto: Los Arcángeles don't give warnings either. That's the only thing we have in common.
